\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Definitions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpThresholds.Definitions
\section{Overview}
Biased probabilities and coordinate symmetries describe threshold curves of increasing Boolean functions. Boosters and pseudo-juntas describe local information on arbitrary finite probability products.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Signed mean booster]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsBooster}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $T\subseteq[n]$, $x\in\Omega$, and $\tau\in\mathbb R$. The restriction $(T,x)$ is a $\tau$-booster if either $\tau>0$ and $\mathbb E_Pf+\tau\le E_Tf(x)$, or $\tau<0$ and $E_Tf(x)\le\mathbb E_Pf+\tau$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Triggered coordinate set]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudoJuntaCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, sets $J_j\subseteq[n]$ and tests $b_j:\Omega\to\{0,1\}$ indexed by $j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Define $J(x)=\bigcup_{j:b_j(x)=1}J_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Triggered coordinate observation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudoJuntaObservation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudoJuntaCoordinates}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, sets $J_j\subseteq[n]$ and tests $b_j:\Omega\to\{0,1\}$ for $j<m$. The observation at $x$ records $x_i$ when $i\in\bigcup_{j:b_j(x)=1}J_j$, and records a distinguished missing symbol otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pseudo-junta predicate]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsPseudoJunta}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudoJuntaCoordinates, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.pseudoJuntaObservation}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $K\in\mathbb R$. Say that $h$ is a $K$-pseudo-junta if there exist finitely many sets $J_j\subseteq[n]$, tests $b_j:\Omega\to\{0,1\}$ depending only on $J_j$, and a real function of the coordinate observations such that $h(x)$ is determined by the values on $J(x)=\bigcup_{j:b_j(x)=1}J_j$, including knowledge of $J(x)$ itself, and $\mathbb E_P|J(x)|\le K$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased event probability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedProbability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeIndicator}
For every $p\in\mathbb R$ and an event $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, define $\Pr_p(A)=\sum_x\prod_i[p\mathbf1_{x_i=1}+(1-p)\mathbf1_{x_i=0}]\mathbf1_A(x)$. For $0\le p\le1$ this is independent Bernoulli-$p$ probability; the formula defines a polynomial for every real $p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Biased output probability curve]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.thresholdCurve}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedProbability}
For every $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ and $p\in\mathbb R$, define $\theta_f(p)=\sum_x\prod_i[p\mathbf1_{x_i=1}+(1-p)\mathbf1_{x_i=0}]\mathbf1_{f(x)=1}$. On $[0,1]$ this is the Bernoulli-$p$ probability of output $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Increasing Boolean functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsIncreasing}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
A function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ is increasing if $x_i\le y_i$ for every coordinate implies $f(x)\le f(y)$, with $0<1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Transitive coordinate symmetry]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsTransitiveSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube}
A function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ is transitively symmetric if for every $i,j\in[n]$ there exists a permutation $\sigma$ of $[n]$ with $\sigma(i)=j$ and $f(x\circ\sigma)=f(x)$ for every $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pivotal probabilities with variance scaling]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedTotalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.biasedProbability}
For every $p\in\mathbb R$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, define $I_p(f)=4p(1-p)\sum_i\Pr_p(f(x^{i\leftarrow0})\ne f(x^{i\leftarrow1}))$, using the polynomial Bernoulli-$p$ weights when $p$ is outside $[0,1]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Labeled simple graph edges]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.GraphEdge}
\leanok
For every $v\in\mathbb N$, the edges on the labeled vertex set $\{0,\ldots,v-1\}$ are its two-element subsets.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Graph-property invariance]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsGraphProperty}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.GraphEdge}
Let $e:[n]\to\binom{[v]}2$ be a bijection and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$. Say that $f$ is a graph property if for every vertex permutation $\sigma$ and inputs $x,y$ satisfying $y_j=x_i$ whenever $e(j)=\sigma(e(i))$, one has $f(y)=f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Monotone disjunctive normal form]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsMonotoneDNF}
\leanok
\uses{DNF}
A disjunctive normal form formula on $n$ Boolean variables is monotone if every literal in every term is a positive variable, without negation.
\end{definition}
